HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 18/08/2023

The instant criminal miscellaneous petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been preferred by the petitioner praying for quashing of FIR No.323/2021 registered at Police Station Hanumangarh Junction, District Hanumangarh, for offences under Sections 420, 406 and 120-B IPC.
As per prosecution, the complainant had one white mare (female horse).
Three persons on 06.06.2021 approached the complainant to buy the white mare, to which the complainant denied.

Afterwards, one of the three persons i.e. co-accused Bahadar Singh who had taken taken the complainant's mobile number, contacted him and told the complainant that he is a broker who had met him during daytime and again asked him to (2 of 8) [CRLMP-3543/2021] sell the mare.

It was further told to the complainant that he (co- accused Bahadar Singh) knows a person/customer from Chandigarh, who had also accompanied him during daytime is thinking/planing of opening a stud farm (farm for selective breeding of livestock), by selling a piece of land.
Co-accused Bahadar Singh also told that the person from Chandigarh would give a good price for the complainant's mare, but this proposal was rejected by the complainant.
The next day, the complainant was again asked by co- accused Bahadar Singh (broker) that he would get good price for the mare.

The complainant after many requests being made, agreed to sell Jaswinder Singh vs State on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140201221/

sentences.text: his mare for Rs.20,75,000, reached after negotiations between the parties

. On 8.6.2021, co-accused Bahadar Singh (broker) told the complainant that the grandfather of the customer/person from Chandigarh is seriously ill and he will will make the payment for the sale of mare in 2-3 days.

On 09.06.2021, co-accused Bahadar Singh (broker) contacted the complainant through mobile and informed that the person from Chandigarh is looking for a black Rajasthani horse for his stud farm and asked the complainant, if he could help in finding the horse and for the same, he would be paid commission.

The complainant on his mobile phone received a photo of a black coloured horse from co-accused Bahadar Singh (broker) who told that the horse is for sale in Wara Daraka village in Punjab, and asked the complainant to come there.

The complainant thereupon, after persistent requests being made by the co-accused Bahadar Singh (broker), came to Wara Daraka and there, the complainant (3 of 8) [CRLMP-3543/2021] met petitioner- Jaswinder Singh, son of Nirmal Singh who told himself to be the owner of the black horse.
Co-accused Bahadar Singh (broker) finalised the deal with the petitioner for an amount of Rs.22 lakhs and paid a sum of Rs.5 lakhs in cash to the petitioner.

The complainant was then informed by co-accused Bahadar Singh (broker) that he may keep the horse in his home and in future, one-two horses or more will be bought and all these horses would be kept at his home from where, they will transport them to Chandigarh.
The complainant was assured that he will be paid commission for his services.

The complainant got influenced by co-accused Bahadar Singh (broker) and upon his asking, sent his son Hardeep Singh in Bolero Camper from Hanumangarh to Wara Daraka for bringing the horse to his home.
Upon which, the complainant son brought the horse.

When the horse was being taken from the house of the petitioner- Jaswinder Singh, the complainant's son was made to sign a stamp paper as an acknowledgment of the delivery of the horse and a photo of complainant with the horse was also captured, under the garb that this would help the complainant's son in avoiding any problem during his journey.

As the horse reached the house of the complainant, both co-accused Bahadar Singh (broker) and petitioner Jaswinder Singh came to the house of the complainant and told that sale of another white horse has been agreed with petitioner- Jaswinder Singh for an amount of 9,50,000 and the same may also be taken by the complainant from Wara Daraka to Hanumangarh.

[CRLMP-3543/2021] The complainant was after some time, informed by co- accused Bahadar Singh (broker) that the grandfather of person/customer living in Chandigarh has passed away and thus, he is unable to send the money for sale of horses, to petitioner- Jaswinder Singh.
The complainant was asked to make payment and he made payment of Rs.26 lakhs to the petitioner- Jaswinder Singh.
The complainant was not contacted by co-accused Bahadar Singh (broker) or by any other co-accused for 2-3 days.

He got suspicious and started enquiring about the worth of the horses,
pursuant to which he came to know that both the horses cost only around Rs. 2- 2.5 lakhs each.

The complainant on coming to know about the worth of the horses, contacted co-accused Bahadar Singh (broker) who gave the phone to petitioner Jaswinder Singh and it was told by the petitioner that he has stamp papers signed by the complainant's son along with pictures of the horse with complainant's son as proof of sale of horses and he further told the complainant that he had the Jaswinder Singh vs State on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140201221/
2 intention of cheating the complainant and grabbing his money.
The offences alleged against the petitioner are under Sections 420, 406, 120B IPC.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the proceedings initiated against the petitioner is nothing but an abuse of process of law.
Learned counsel further submitted that a civil matter has been given a colour of criminal case by the complainant, only with a view to rope the petitioner in a false criminal case.

Learned counsel submitted that the present F.I.R.
(5 of 8) [CRLMP-3543/2021] has been filed/lodged with malafide intention, after framing a concocted story based on manipulated facts.

Learned counsel submitted that as a matter of fact, the petitioner had sold a black horse and a white mare to the complainant which is fortified from the documents annexed to the present miscellaneous petition.

It was thus, prayed that F.I.R.
No.323/2021, registered at PS Hanumangarh Junction, District Hanumangarh may kindly be quashed and set aside.

Learned Public Prosecutor while opposing the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the petitioner, submitted that thorough investigation has been conducted by the investigating agency and it has been found that the petitioner is the main accused in the matter.
It was urged that the offence charged against the petitioner are cognizable offences which has been found proved by the investigating agency after conducting due investigation.
It was submitted that the documents relied upon by the counsel for the petitioner, the genuineness of the same will be looked into during investigation.
Learned

Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant urged that the allegations made in the F.I.R. clearly disclose commission of a cognizable offence and therefore, the statutory power of police to register an F.I.R. and investigate the matter cannot be said to be an abuse of process of law.

It was also submitted that the court should not interfere with the investigation, particularly when the investigating agency, on the basis of material collected during investigation has found the charges/allegations to be proved against the petitioners.

[CRLMP-3543/2021] Reliance was placed on the judgment of Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana vs. Bhajan Lal & Ors. reported in 1992 Supp. (1) SCC 335, wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has illustrated the situations wherein, the extraordinary powers under Article 226 of the Constitution of India or the inherent powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C. can be exercised by the High Court either to prevent abuse of the process of any Court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice.

sentences.text: Learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant thus, prayed that the criminal miscellaneous petition deserves to be rejected by this Court.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant.
Perused the material available on record.
This Court had directed learned Public Prosecutor to procure the case diary.
In compliance of the order, learned Public Prosecutor has produced the case diary along with the factual report of the case for this Court's kind perusal.
After perusing the case diary, this Court finds that cognizable offences are made out against the petitioner.
It is well settled that the Court while exercising its powers under Section 482 CrPC cannot decide the correctness of the allegations levelled against accused persons.

This Court is of the opinion that at this stage, it is neither appropriate to scan the entire material produced before it nor record its definite findings, after examining the documents/material, for quashing the impugned FIR.
In the result, petitioner has failed to make out a prima facie case warranting exercise of powers under Section 482 CrPC for quashment of the F.I.R. in question.
